gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much screen each sub-2 lb extender gives per pound: about 58 sq in per lb for the 13.3-inch Duex Plus DS, 56 for the SideTrak Swivel 14, 51 for the Duex Lite and 47 for the Duex Max DS, with the Max DS adding 12% more screen for 38% more weight.
standout_why: I opened thedadsneeze.com (rank 12) and PCWorld Shop (cited). thedadsneeze lists raw weights (1.3 lb, 1.8 lb, 1.87 lb) and a range ('add 1.3 to 2.3 pounds') but computes no per-area, per-pound or laptop-plus-screen figure. PCWorld Shop gives only the Duex Lite's 1.3 lb and dimensions. ChatGPT's own answer already says the Plus DS 'leaves 0.7 lb for accessories', so headroom under the line is not new. mobilepixels.us (cited) and thexebec.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, through both WebFetch and storecheck.py, so I could not compare against them or read the maker's weights. The 1.3 lb and 1.8 lb inputs therefore rest on thedadsneeze, not on Mobile Pixels, and every derived figure for those two models is conditional on re-reading them.
decides: It confirms the Duex Plus DS as the pick if Mobile Pixels' 1.3 lb holds: it ties the Duex Lite for lightest, gives 13% more screen at the same weight, and has the most screen per pound of the attached screens. The Duex Max DS is the 'bigger screen, still under the line' row, with only 3.2 oz of headroom. One thing could overturn this: a search snippet of Mobile Pixels' own Duex Plus DS manual appeared to pair 13.3 in with 1.8 lb. I could not open the PDF to check, and if the manual does say 1.8 lb, the Plus DS loses its weight lead over the Max DS and the 1.5 lb SideTrak Swivel 14 becomes the lightest 14-inch-class row.
